title: STAGGER: Enabling All-in-One Subarray Sensing for Efficient Module-level Processing in Open-Bitline ReRAM
problem: Peripheral separated sample-and-holds and ADCs for row buffering and sensing in conventional ReRAM designs create a system bottleneck. Sequential readout of multiple-bit results from the same bitline during vector-matrix-multiplication wastes latency and energy.
motivation: ReRAM devices can achieve energy-efficient in-memory scientific computing through in-situ VMM, but realizing this potential requires eliminating the sensing and buffering bottleneck in the datapath.
method: Instead of separate analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), sensing happens directly in the ReRAM array using PORM (precharge once, readout multiple-bits), which reads multiple result bits from a single bitline by overlapping their timing—taking advantage of the fact that high-order and low-order bits complete at slightly different times to read them nearly simultaneously. A cascaded-feedback sensing circuit and sense amplifier positioned directly on the memory cells prevent conflicts between different bit accesses. By interleaving successive column readouts, hardware utilization improves, reducing latency.
key_novelty: PORM (precharge once, readout multiple-bits) enables reading multiple result bits from a single bitline precharge by overlapping the timing of different-significance bits.
contributions: ADC-less all-in-one processing-in-ReRAM design eliminating peripheral sensing bottleneck
PORM mechanism for efficient overlapped multi-bit readout from shared bitlines
Cascaded-feedback bitline sensing architecture with decoupled sense amplifier design
Cross-level interleaving mechanism for optimized spatiotemporal hardware utilization
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations; applicability beyond VMM workloads and scaling properties not addressed.
primary_theme: Efficient ReRAM sensing for in-memory vector-matrix-multiplication
